controls: Gate the vector path behind a zvfhmin-capability check and keep the scalar ryg helper as the reference and fallback.

Build a bit-exact conformance test comparing vector vs scalar ryg output across the full special-value corpus (NaN payloads, ±Inf, ±0, denormals, 65504/65520 boundaries, half-ties) before any perf comparison.
Add a short-vector crossover (use scalar below a measured d threshold) and re-measure the 20-iteration QT_fp16 benchmark after landing.
Verify one vsetvl per main-loop interval with no vtype switching inside; count header has zero vector spills.
reasons: Zvfhmin vfncvt.f.f.w rounding/NaN canonicalization and denormal handling may differ from the ryg bit-trick (qNaN 0x7E00, Inf 0x7C00, denormals via FP32 denormals): mismatches would silently change stored codes unless repaired on the masked special lanes.
Vectorization changes the encode's numerical path (FRM, FTZ, NaN payload) which affects downstream distance computations; any bit-pattern deviation changes index results, not just speed.
A fixed 16-bit store stream requires vse16 alignment/layout identical to the ((uint16_t*)code) contract; an LMUL or SEW mismatch could corrupt adjacent code entries.
If SIMDLevel<0> exists specifically to provide a scalar/reference path, unconditional vectorization could regress short-vector calls or duplicate maintenance.

conditions.description: Target build and hardware expose zvfhmin (build tag already carries v1p0 zve64f zvfhmin zvl128b); verify at runtime and fall back to scalar ryg otherwise.
QuantizerFP16 must continue producing the exact scalar ryg bit patterns for NaN payloads, ±0, ±Inf, denormals, overflow/underflow, and half-tie rounding.
Vector cost amortizes: only take the vector path for d where vsetvli + lane-repair setup pays (benchmark d gives 128 floats / 256-byte codes) with a short-input scalar crossover.
v type stability: e32 main loop, source fractional LMUL from destination LMUL budget per the widening/narrowing rule; no per-element vtype churn or vector spills.

actions.proposal: Replace the inlined scalar ryg encode_fp16 loop in QuantizerFP16<0>::encode_vector (quantizers.h:246) with a stable-vtype RVV narrowing fast path when zvfhmin is available: vsetvl e32, vle32.v load of the float block, a masked detect of special lanes (NaN / ±Inf / boundary), vfncvt.f.f.w (Zvfhmin f32->f16 narrowing, RNE through FRM) on the bulk lanes, a masked repair that writes the scalar ryg bit patterns (qNaN 0x7E00|sign, Inf 0x7C00|sign) only on special lanes, then vse16.v to the uint16_t code buffer; keep the untouched ryg encode_fp16 as the invariant scalar fallback and for the residual tail/SIMDLevel-0 path.

correctness_checks: Bit-exact lane comparison with scalar ryg encode_fp16 for a corpus of random floats plus NaN (qNaN/sNaN with varied payloads), ±Inf, ±0, denormals, largest/smallest normal, 65504/65520 overflow boundaries, and half-integer ties; zero mismatches.

Inspect disassembly: the encode loop must contain vle32/vfncvt/vse16 and zero scalar special-value branches except in the masked repair block; vsetvli appears once per iteration interval, not per element.
Confirm FRM is stable (RNE) and any FTZ difference is limited to the repair path; validate a decode_vector round-trip on stored codes against the scalar reference.

expected_signals.signal: The scalar special-value branches and bit-manipulation chain (bltu a6,a3 NaN path, beq a3,a6 Inf path, fmv.w.x/fmul.s/flt.s/fmv.x.w) disappear from the hot encode-loop interval except inside the masked repair block.
v*/vfncvt.f.f.w/vsetvli/vle32/vse16 mnemonics appear in the encode-loop disassembly and carry the bulk of samples in the new profile.
perf stat instruction count of the sq-encode testcase decreases while its duration_time stays constant or shrinks; L1/LLC miss rates remain low (compute-bound).
The special-lane masked slow path share rises only when the float input corpus contains NaN/Inf/boundary values, confirming the fast path handles the common case.

success_criteria: Per-element dynamic instructions in the encode loop fall well under the current ~18-instruction scalar body (perf stat -e instructions on an isolated fixed-length sq-encode run).
benchmark_QT_fp16_real_time_ns drops below the 993,739 ns baseline and trends toward the bf16 (482,281 ns) and 8bit_direct (392,277 ns) encode timings for equal d.
The new iterated profile shows the loop dominated by vsetvli/vle/vfncvt/vse (bulk) with only a narrow masked repair interval remaining.
No fp16 encode throughput regression at the 20-iteration benchmark for the scalar fallback configuration.

controls: Measure instructions/cycles before and after with perf stat on a fixed iteration count and diff disassembly for new spill/reload instructions in the loop.
Scope the change to the scalar path only and re-verify the primary guidance's vector path when it lands.
If no compiler knob is available, accept the conservative rematerialization and rely on the vector rewrite instead.
reasons: Keeping 0x7E00 live across the loop body can raise register pressure and introduce a spill that negates the gain (2 of ~18 instructions, i.e., <12% ceiling).
Register-allocation and rematerialization decisions are compiler-version- and optimization-level-specific; a forced hint can shift unrelated scheduling heuristically.

conditions.description: Applies only while the scalar ryg loop remains the deployed path (SIMDLevel-0 / no zvfhmin / short d), since the vector rewrite removes the loop body itself.
The actual mechanism depends on the compiler's register-allocation choice that merged the invariant constant with the conversion-result register a5.
No new loop-live value may force a spill/reload elsewhere in the body that would outweigh the ~2-instruction saving.

actions.proposal: Eliminate the per-iteration rematerialization of the loop-invariant fp16 NaN constant 0x7E00 in the scalar encode loop: hold 0x7E00 in a dedicated live-though-loop register (or restructure encode_fp16 so the NaN/Inf constants are computed once before the loop and reused), removing the lui a5,0x8 / addi a5,a5,-512 pair from the ~18-instruction loop body when the scalar path is retained; the RVV narrowing rewrite of the primary root cause subsumes this entirely.

correctness_checks: fp16 output bytes remain bit-identical to the reference ryg encode_fp16 for the special-value corpus (NaN payloads, ±Inf, ±0, denormals, ties) after the constant hoist.
Compare before/after disassembly to verify the constant appears exactly once and no register spill/reload was added inside the loop.

expected_signals.signal: lui a5,0x8 + addi a5,a5,-512 (0x3895c8-0x3895ca) disappears from the per-iteration body; the constant is materialized once in the pre-loop setup.
perf stat -e instructions for the encode loopion of the sq-encode workload drops by roughly 2 per element with no increase in spill/load samples.
If implemented via a compiler RA/liverange directive, generated code shows the 0x7E00 value held in a stable register across iterations.
The encode output bit patterns and the rest of the scalar loop body (fmul/clamp/shift/sign-pack sequence) stay unchanged.

success_criteria: Disassembly shows the 0x7E00 constant formed once before the loop (single lui/addi at loop setup) and zero lui/addi materializations inside the loop body.
Instruction count per element drops by ~2 with no additional spill/reload instructions introduced in the loop.
The luI/addw hotspots (0x3895c8/0x3895f2) no longer appear as per-iteration instructions in the retained-scalar annotate.

gaps.description: The cpu-clock annotate for this function contains only 2 samples; the 50%/50% per-instruction shares are statistically weak and the function's share of the whole sq-encode benchmark duration is unknown, so the benefit ceiling is directional, not quantified.

Sampling-IP precision (precise_ip / Exact-IP / PMU skid) is not reported for cpu-clock; the two instruction-level hotspots are therefore sound only at basic-block/loop-interval granularity, not as per-instruction latency claims.

Hardware ISA and VLEN are not directly measured; only the build's Tag_RISCV_arch (zvl128b, zvfhmin1p0) is known, so the actual vlenb and the in-harness LMUL/throughput of a vector conversion path are unverified.

Core microarchitecture (in-order vs out-of-order, FP-unit latency, FMV transfer cost) is unidentified; the unresolved alternative (scalar FP dependency latency vs instruction/branch count as the limiter) cannot be settled without it.

Zvfhmin vfncvt.f.f.w behavior on this silicon (rounding mode, FTZ/denormal semantics, NaN canonicalization vs ryg qNaN 0x7E00) is unverified, leaving the masked special-lane repair envelope provisional until hardware-checked.

review_items.description: Re-profile with a higher sample count (perf record -F <higher freq> -e cpu-clock on sq-encode) and re-annotate; or isolate the encode_vector call in a microbenchmark to obtain a stable per-element cycle count.
Collect with a PMU event supporting precise IP sampling (or record perf's skid/precise_ip setting) so instruction-level attribution is interval-confirmed.
On the target read /proc/cpuinfo isa, query riscv_hwprobe, and read the vlenb CSR (or /sys/.../vlenb) to confirm VLEN>=128b and zvfhmin presence at runtime.
Identify the core (lh /proc/cpuinfo model string) and collect a dedicated cycle/instruction annotate on a minimal encode loop to separate dependency-latency from instruction-slot effects.

Run a small RVV conformance probe comparing vfncvt f32->f16 bit outputs (NaN payload, ±0, ±Inf, denormal, tie cases) against the ryg reference on the actual hardware before sizing the repair slow path.

alternative_explanations.explanation: The scalar dependency chain fmv.w.x->fmul.s->flt.s->fmv.x.w->addw plus FMV transfer latency carries each element's conversion; on an unknown (in-order vs OOO) core this could make a latency-bound rather than instruction/branch-bound loop. It does not change the fix direction (vector conversion removes the whole chain) but raises uncertainty on the exact magnitude.

The two samples could both be anchored by the per-iteration setup/rounding instructions of the scalar encode (the 'lui 0x7E00' materialization and rounding add) rather than by stall cycles; the constant-rematerialization detail is captured as a separate contributing factor and the vector rewrite eliminates it together with the branches.

NaN/Inf branch mispredictions could in principle dominate, but global branch_miss_rate is 0.388% and fp16 encode inputs are typically benign finite norms, so data-dependent special-value branches are not the main cost driver.

findings.conclusion: QuantizerFP16<SIMDLevel0>::encode_vector's hot region is the inlined scalar FP32->FP16 encode_fp16 (faiss/utils/fp16-inl.h:32 ryg integer/FP trick, invoked per element from quantizers.h:246): every element runs per-lane bit extraction, NaN/Inf special-value branches (bltu/beq -> 0x7E00 NaN / 0x7C00 Inf), FP-multiply rescale (fmul.s), rounding add+arithmetic shift, sign pack and 2-byte store. Both in-function hotspots (0x3895c8 lui 50%, 0x3895f2 addw 50%) are inside that chain, and zero v* (no vfncvt/vfwcvt) conversion instructions execute even though libfaiss is built for v1p0+zve64f+zvfhmin+zvl128b, so the required precision conversion repeats all scalar special-value/rounding machinery per element in a compute-bound loop (IPC 0.83, L1 miss 0.357%, branch miss 0.388%).

neighbor_exclusions.reason: The FP32->FP16 conversion is required by the QuantizerFP16 output code contract (quantizers.h writes uint16_t code); this is not a redundant float32/float64 round trip, so the unnecessary-conversion row's premise fails.

The hot work is a dtype conversion dominated by per-lane special-value/rounding handling, not same-lane compare/select or x*scale+bias arithmetic; precision-conversion semantics own the sample range 0x3895c6-0x38960e.
No matmul/GEMV structure exists; conversion is the whole kernel and not an input or epilogue of an FP operator, so the matmul row does not apply.

findings.reasoning: Disassembly of the target (35e73ea6) shows the whole loop 0x3895c6-0x38960e is the inlined encode_fp16 with constants hoisted outside the loop (t1/t4/t5/t3/a6/fa3/fa4) but data-dependent scalar special-value handling per element; hotspot packet (e9d2d827) attributes 50%+50% to the lui a5,0x8 and addw a5,a5,t5 lines in that body. Source read (69dfcac7) confirms encode_fp16 performs fint&round_mask, floatbits(magic) FP multiply, min clamp, intbits-0x1000 rounding and >>13, with NaN->0x7E00 and Inf->0x7C00 overrides (fp16-inl.h:32-58); quantizers.h:246 confirms the per-dimension scalar loop. Metadata read (e58ba58f) shows the libfaiss build carries v1p0, zve64f1p0, zvfhmin1p0, zvl128b1p0, so a bulk vfncvt.f.f.w narrowing path (plus masked NaN/Inf repair) is a proven lane-independent formulation per rvv_precision_conversion_kernels; perf_stat (1e2d216d) shows IPC 0.83 and negligible cache-miss/branch-miss rates, i.e., compute-bound scalar encode dominates.

alternative_explanations.explanation: Reusing a5 may minimize register pressure and avoid a callee-saved spill elsewhere; holding 0x7E00 in a dedicated register could cost an extra living value in the loop, so the net instruction saving is bounded (~2 of 18 instructions) and the vector rewrite makes it moot.

Materializing only inside the NaN branch would require splitting the merge at 0x3895fc, which the compiler avoided for a branch-heavy layout; unconditional setup is a conservative scheduling decision rather than an outright optimizer defect.

findings.conclusion: Within the scalar loop the single most-sampled instruction (0x3895c8 lui a5,0x8, 50% of in-function samples) is the first half of per-iteration rematerialization of the loop-invariant fp16 NaN constant 0x7E00 (lui a5,0x8; addi a5,a5,-512). The compiler hoisted all other loop-invariant constants (0x7fffffff, 0x7f800000, 0x8000, 0x1000, 0x7ffff000, float magic, clamp max) out of the loop but reuses a5 for the conversion result, forcing 2 extra instructions per ~18-instruction iteration.

neighbor_exclusions.reason: No constant-pool load or rodata/frontend footprint dominates: the fp16 NaN constant 0x7E00 is already ALU-materialized (lui+addi), so the constant-load-from-memory mechanism this row addresses is not present.

The loop already uses precomputed end-pointer + pointer increments (addi a1,a1,4/addi a2,a2,2 + single bne); the observed inefficiency is register reuse of a loop-invariant constant, not index-scaling in the induction trace.
The redundant per-iteration 0x7E00 setup is a loop-invariant hoist/RA problem, not an algebraically removable NEG+MUL, extension, or tag-bit peephole inside a straight-line sequence.

findings.reasoning: The annotate (35e73ea6) shows constants t1/a6/t4/t5/t3/fa3/fa4 initialized once at 0x3895ae-0x3895c4 while a5=0x7E00 is rebuilt at 0x3895c8-0x3895ca on every pass; the loop merge at 0x3895fc consumes a5 from three definitions (regular conversion, NaN, Inf) so the compiler chose unconditional re-materialization. hotspot packet (e9d2d827) ranks 0x3895c8 as top sample. This is a compiler code-generation shape (register allocation merges the invariant with the scratch register), not a semantic necessity.

asm.reason: No handwritten assembly: disassembly is entirely compiler-generated scalar RISC-V (lw/fmul/mv/sh loop) with zero v* or hand-SIMD mnemonics; no .S provenance or independent-carrier policy signal exists for this function.

codegen.reason: Compiler-generated scalar loop hotspot 0x3895c8 lui a5,0x8 (50%) recomputes loop-invariant constant 0x7e00 via lui+addi every iteration; 0x3895f2 addw (50%) is the contiguous rounding step in the serial encode_fp16 chain. Instruction-form/constant-materialization inefficiency is an in-scope codegen signal.

crypto.reason: No cryptographic primitive appears; the encoded loop is generic fp32->fp16 bit manipulation (AES/SHA/SM/CRC/GF terms absent).

offload.reason: No matrix engine, packed-SIMD-within-GPR, weight repacking, im2col, or GEMM structure exists; workload is element-wise precision conversion, routed to operator_rvv instead.

operator_rvv.reason: Compiler-generated scalar operator loop (elementwise f32->f16 precision conversion) with proven lane-independent RVV formulation: build has zve64f/zvfhmin v1p0 and a per-lane vfncvt.f.f.w conversion is available at VLEN 128; profile is compute-bound scalar (IPC 0.83) entirely inside the encode loop.

runtime_os.reason: No timer, interrupt, privileged-CSR, or runtime-context activity in the hotspot; pure user-space element loop.

string_memory.reason: Hotspot is ALU/FM value-conversion work, not copy/fill/sentinel/checksum/comparison; L1_dcache_load_miss_rate 0.357% and branch_miss_rate 0.388% show loads/stores are not the bottleneck.

vectorized_tuning.reason: Class requires annotated output already containing v*; target output has zero vector instructions, so there is no RVV configuration/unrolling/bookkeeping to tune (scalar-causes handled by codegen/operator_rvv).
